  1 | #!/usr/bin/env python3
  2 | """Add token-level enriched columns to an existing enriched parquet dataset.
  3 | 
  4 | Reads local parquet shards, preserves existing columns, and writes a sibling
  5 | dataset with token_ids plus token-level enriched metadata columns materialized
  6 | offline. This is intended for A/B dataloader benchmarking against the legacy
  7 | char-level parquet path without round-tripping through JSONL again.
  8 | """
  9 | 
 10 | from __future__ import annotations
 11 | 
 12 | import argparse
 13 | import json
 14 | import os
 15 | from pathlib import Path
 16 | 
 17 | import pyarrow as pa  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
 18 | import pyarrow.parquet as pq  # type: ignore[import-not-found]
 19 | 
 20 | from cppmega_mlx.tokenizer.cpp_tokenizer import load_cppmega_tokenizer
 21 | from cppmega_mlx.data.nanochat_pipeline.tokenized_enriched import materialize_tokenized_enriched_batch
 22 | from cppmega_mlx.data.nanochat_pipeline.tokenized_enriched_schema import TOKENIZED_ENRICHED_COLUMNS
 23 | 
 24 | 
 25 | def _decode_json_like(value):
 26 |     while isinstance(value, str) and value:
 27 |         decoded = json.loads(value)
 28 |         if decoded == value:
 29 |             break
 30 |         value = decoded
 31 |     return value
 32 | 
 33 | 
 34 | def _list_parquet_files(input_dir: str) -> list[Path]:
 35 |     return sorted(
 36 |         Path(input_dir).glob("*.parquet"),
 37 |         key=lambda p: p.name,
 38 |     )
 39 | 
 40 | 
 41 | def _table_to_docs(table: pa.Table) -> list[dict]:
 42 |     columns = {name: table.column(name).to_pylist() for name in table.column_names}
 43 |     num_rows = table.num_rows
 44 |     docs = []
 45 |     for i in range(num_rows):
 46 |         row = {name: values[i] for name, values in columns.items()}
 47 |         for json_list_field in ("chunk_boundaries", "call_edges", "type_edges"):
 48 |             value = row.get(json_list_field)
 49 |             if value is None:
 50 |                 continue
 51 |             value = _decode_json_like(value)
 52 |             if isinstance(value, list):
 53 |                 value = [_decode_json_like(item) for item in value]
 54 |             row[json_list_field] = value
 55 |         for json_obj_field in ("platform_info", "language_info", "build_info"):
 56 |             value = row.get(json_obj_field)
 57 |             if value is None:
 58 |                 continue
 59 |             row[json_obj_field] = _decode_json_like(value)
 60 |         docs.append(row)
 61 |     return docs
 62 | 
 63 | 
 64 | def _merge_table_with_tokenized(
 65 |     table: pa.Table,
 66 |     tokenized_rows: list[dict],
 67 | ) -> pa.Table:
 68 |     base_columns = {name: table.column(name) for name in table.column_names}
 69 |     for column_name in TOKENIZED_ENRICHED_COLUMNS:
 70 |         base_columns[column_name] = pa.array(
 71 |             [row.get(column_name, []) for row in tokenized_rows]
 72 |         )
 73 |     return pa.table(base_columns)
 74 | 
 75 | 
 76 | def _copy_metadata_files(input_dir: str, output_dir: str) -> None:
 77 |     for name in ("_COMPLETE",):
 78 |         src = Path(input_dir) / name
 79 |         if src.exists():
 80 |             Path(output_dir, name).write_text(src.read_text())
 81 | 
 82 | 
 83 | def main() -> None:
 84 |     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
 85 |     parser.add_argument("--input-dir", required=True)
 86 |     parser.add_argument("--output-dir", required=True)
 87 |     parser.add_argument(
 88 |         "--max-files",
 89 |         type=int,
 90 |         default=0,
 91 |         help="Only process the first N parquet shards (0 = all).",
 92 |     )
 93 |     parser.add_argument(
 94 |         "--tokenizer-path",
 95 |         default="",
 96 |         help="Optional tokenizer.json path used for token materialization.",
 97 |     )
 98 |     parser.add_argument(
 99 |         "--row-group-size",
100 |         type=int,
101 |         default=1024,
102 |         help="Row group size for rewritten output shards.",
103 |     )
104 |     args = parser.parse_args()
105 | 
106 |     os.makedirs(args.output_dir, exist_ok=True)
107 |     parquet_files = _list_parquet_files(args.input_dir)
108 |     if args.max_files > 0:
109 |         parquet_files = parquet_files[: args.max_files]
110 |     if not parquet_files:
111 |         raise FileNotFoundError(f"No parquet files found under {args.input_dir}")
112 | 
113 |     tokenizer_path = args.tokenizer_path
114 |     if not tokenizer_path:
115 |         raise ValueError("--tokenizer-path is required for parquet materialization")
116 |     tokenizer = load_cppmega_tokenizer(tokenizer_path)
117 | 
118 |     for idx, src_path in enumerate(parquet_files, 1):
119 |         dst_path = Path(args.output_dir) / src_path.name
120 |         print(f"[{idx}/{len(parquet_files)}] {src_path.name}")
121 |         table = pq.read_table(src_path)
122 |         docs = _table_to_docs(table)
123 |         tokenized_rows = materialize_tokenized_enriched_batch(docs, tokenizer)
124 |         merged = _merge_table_with_tokenized(table, tokenized_rows)
125 |         pq.write_table(
126 |             merged,
127 |             dst_path,
128 |             row_group_size=args.row_group_size,
129 |             compression="snappy",
130 |         )
131 | 
132 |     _copy_metadata_files(args.input_dir, args.output_dir)
133 |     print(f"Wrote tokenized parquet dataset to {args.output_dir}")
134 | 
135 | 
136 | if __name__ == "__main__":
137 |     main()
```

 1 | #!/bin/bash
 2 | # megacpp master data prep dispatcher.
 3 | #
 4 | # Runs download -> tokenize -> format -> cache -> verify to produce the
 5 | # Megatron-format ``clang_semantic_4k_v10`` dataset used by NAM56R training
 6 | # (see scripts/remote_smoke_h200_dsa_9_4_m.sh).
 7 | #
 8 | # See docs/data_preparation.md for full details.
 9 | #
10 | # Usage:
11 | #   bash prepare_data.sh                # run all stages
12 | #   bash prepare_data.sh download       # just clone source repos
13 | #   bash prepare_data.sh tokenize       # requires MEGACPP_NANOCHAT_ROOT
14 | #   bash prepare_data.sh format         # parquet -> Megatron .bin/.idx
15 | #   bash prepare_data.sh cache          # warm/validate index cache
16 | #   bash prepare_data.sh verify         # sanity-check final dataset
17 | #
18 | # Env knobs (all optional):
19 | #   MEGACPP_DATA_ROOT    default: /home/dave/cppmega-root/data
20 | #   MEGACPP_DATASET_NAME default: clang_semantic_4k_v10
21 | #   MEGACPP_NANOCHAT_ROOT  (required for 'tokenize' stage)
22 | 
23 | set -euo pipefail
24 | 
25 | HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
26 | PY="${PYTHON:-python3}"
27 | 
28 | STAGE="${1:-all}"
29 | 
30 | run_download() {
31 |     bash "$HERE/prepare_download_megacpp.sh"
32 | }
33 | run_tokenize() {
34 |     "$PY" "$HERE/prepare_tokenize_megacpp.py"
35 | }
36 | run_format() {
37 |     "$PY" "$HERE/prepare_format_megacpp.py"
38 | }
39 | run_cache() {
40 |     "$PY" "$HERE/prepare_cache_megacpp.py"
41 | }
42 | run_verify() {
43 |     "$PY" "$HERE/verify_dataset_megacpp.py"
44 | }
45 | 
46 | case "$STAGE" in
47 |     download) run_download ;;
48 |     tokenize) run_tokenize ;;
49 |     format)   run_format ;;
50 |     cache)    run_cache ;;
51 |     verify)   run_verify ;;
52 |     all)
53 |         run_download
54 |         run_tokenize
55 |         run_format
56 |         run_cache
57 |         run_verify
58 |         ;;
59 |     *)
60 |         echo "usage: $0 {download|tokenize|format|cache|verify|all}" >&2
61 |         exit 2
62 |         ;;
63 | esac

 1 | #!/bin/bash
 2 | # megacpp data prep — Stage 1: Download raw C/C++ source corpora.
 3 | #
 4 | # Adopted from nanochat/scripts/data/download_cpp_sources.sh.
 5 | # Clones a fixed set of C/C++ repositories used as the megacpp training corpus
 6 | # foundation. No credentials required — all sources are public GitHub repos.
 7 | #
 8 | # Sibling stages: see scripts/data/prepare_data.sh.
 9 | #
10 | # Usage:
11 | #   bash prepare_download_megacpp.sh [DATA_DIR]
12 | #
13 | # Default DATA_DIR: ${MEGACPP_DATA_ROOT:-/home/dave/cppmega-root/data}/cpp_raw
14 | #
15 | # Output: ${DATA_DIR} containing shallow clones of each repo.

  1 | """megacpp data prep helper — stream a growing JSONL into parquet shards.
  2 | 
  3 | Adopted verbatim from nanochat/scripts/data/stream_jsonl_to_parquet.py (no
  4 | ``nanochat.*`` imports — self-contained). Renamed with the megacpp suffix and
  5 | default paths aligned with ``MEGACPP_DATA_ROOT``.
  6 | 
  7 | Reads from a JSONL file that is still being written to, and produces parquet
  8 | shards as documents accumulate. Watches for the JSONL writer to finish (no new
  9 | data for 60s + file not growing), then writes the final validation shard and a
 10 | ``_COMPLETE`` sentinel.
 11 | 
 12 | Usage:
 13 |     python prepare_stream_jsonl_to_parquet_megacpp.py \
 14 |         --input  /path/to/cpp_chunked_all.jsonl \
 15 |         --parquet_dir /path/to/parquet/clang_semantic_4k_v10 \
 16 |         --rows_per_file 50000
 17 | """
 18 | import argparse
 19 | import json
 20 | import os
 21 | import random
 22 | import time
 23 | 
 24 | import pyarrow as pa
 25 | import pyarrow.parquet as pq
 26 | 
 27 | 
 28 | def main():
 29 |     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
 30 |     parser.add_argument("--input", required=True, help="Input JSONL (may still be growing)")
 31 |     parser.add_argument("--parquet_dir", required=True, help="Output parquet directory")
 32 |     parser.add_argument("--rows_per_file", type=int, default=50000)
 33 |     parser.add_argument("--val_fraction", type=float, default=0.01)
 34 |     parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=42)
 35 |     args = parser.parse_args()
 36 | 
 37 |     os.makedirs(args.parquet_dir, exist_ok=True)
 38 |     rng = random.Random(args.seed)
 39 | 
 40 |     shard_idx = 0
 41 |     batch = []
 42 |     total_docs = 0
 43 |     stale_count = 0
 44 |     last_pos = 0
 45 | 
 46 |     print(f"[megacpp_stream_pq] Watching {args.input} -> {args.parquet_dir}")
 47 |     print(f"[megacpp_stream_pq] Rows per shard: {args.rows_per_file}")
 48 | 
 49 |     while not os.path.exists(args.input):
 50 |         print(f"[megacpp_stream_pq] Waiting for {args.input}...")
 51 |         time.sleep(10)
 52 | 
 53 |     with open(args.input) as f:
 54 |         while True:
 55 |             line = f.readline()
 56 |             if not line:
 57 |                 current_size = os.path.getsize(args.input)
 58 |                 if current_size == last_pos:
 59 |                     stale_count += 1
 60 |                 else:
 61 |                     stale_count = 0
 62 |                     last_pos = current_size
 63 |                 if stale_count >= 4:
 64 |                     print("[megacpp_stream_pq] Input file stable for 60s, finishing up")
 65 |                     break
 66 |                 time.sleep(15)
 67 |                 continue
 68 | 
 69 |             stale_count = 0
 70 |             line = line.strip()
 71 |             if not line:
 72 |                 continue
 73 | 
 74 |             text = json.loads(line)["text"]
 75 |             batch.append(text)
 76 |             total_docs += 1
 77 | 
 78 |             if len(batch) >= args.rows_per_file:
 79 |                 rng.shuffle(batch)
 80 |                 table = pa.table({"text": batch})
 81 |                 path = os.path.join(args.parquet_dir, f"shard_{shard_idx:05d}.parquet")
 82 |                 pq.write_table(table, path, row_group_size=1024)
 83 |                 try:
 84 |                     pf = pq.ParquetFile(path)
 85 |                     assert pf.num_row_groups > 0, f"Empty parquet: {path}"
 86 |                     pf.read_row_group(0)
 87 |                 except Exception as e:
 88 |                     print(f"[ERROR] Corrupt parquet written, removing: {path} - {e}")
 89 |                     os.remove(path)
 90 |                     raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to write valid parquet: {path}") from e
 91 |                 print(
 92 |                     f"[megacpp_stream_pq] Written shard_{shard_idx:05d}.parquet "
 93 |                     f"({len(batch)} docs, {total_docs:,} total)"
 94 |                 )
 95 |                 shard_idx += 1
 96 |                 batch = []
 97 | 
 98 |     val_count = max(1, int(total_docs * args.val_fraction))
 99 |     if len(batch) > val_count:
100 |         train_part = batch[:-val_count]
101 |         val_part = batch[-val_count:]
102 |     else:
103 |         train_part = batch
104 |         val_part = []
105 | 
106 |     if train_part:
107 |         rng.shuffle(train_part)
108 |         table = pa.table({"text": train_part})
109 |         path = os.path.join(args.parquet_dir, f"shard_{shard_idx:05d}.parquet")
110 |         pq.write_table(table, path, row_group_size=1024)
111 |         try:
112 |             pf = pq.ParquetFile(path)
113 |             assert pf.num_row_groups > 0, f"Empty parquet: {path}"
114 |             pf.read_row_group(0)
115 |         except Exception as e:
116 |             print(f"[ERROR] Corrupt parquet written, removing: {path} - {e}")
117 |             os.remove(path)
118 |             raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to write valid parquet: {path}") from e
119 |         print(
120 |             f"[megacpp_stream_pq] Written final train shard_{shard_idx:05d}.parquet "
121 |             f"({len(train_part)} docs)"
122 |         )
123 |         shard_idx += 1
124 | 
125 |     if val_part:
126 |         val_table = pa.table({"text": val_part})
127 |         val_path = os.path.join(args.parquet_dir, "val_shard.parquet")
128 |         pq.write_table(val_table, val_path, row_group_size=1024)
129 |         try:
130 |             pf = pq.ParquetFile(val_path)
131 |             assert pf.num_row_groups > 0, f"Empty parquet: {val_path}"
132 |             pf.read_row_group(0)
133 |         except Exception as e:
134 |             print(f"[ERROR] Corrupt parquet written, removing: {val_path} - {e}")
135 |             os.remove(val_path)
136 |             raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to write valid parquet: {val_path}") from e
137 |         print(f"[megacpp_stream_pq] Written val_shard.parquet ({len(val_part)} docs)")
138 | 
139 |     sentinel = os.path.join(args.parquet_dir, "_COMPLETE")
140 |     with open(sentinel, "w") as sf:
141 |         sf.write(f"{shard_idx} train shards, {len(val_part)} val docs, {total_docs} total\n")
142 | 
143 |     print(
144 |         f"[megacpp_stream_pq] DONE: {shard_idx} train shards, "
145 |         f"{total_docs:,} total docs, _COMPLETE written"
146 |     )
147 | 
148 | 
149 | if __name__ == "__main__":
150 |     main()
```

 1 | #!/usr/bin/env python3
 2 | """megacpp data prep — Stage 4: Pre-build Megatron GPTDataset index cache.
 3 | 
 4 | Megatron's ``GPTDataset`` lazily writes a shuffle / sample / document index
 5 | under ``<dataset_prefix>/cache/GPTDataset_indices/`` on first access. For
 6 | large corpora this can add several minutes to the first training launch.
 7 | This stage warms that cache by instantiating the dataset once with the same
 8 | config knobs used at train time.

10 | This is a best-effort helper — on machines without megatron-core installed
11 | (dev laptops) the script prints a clear skip message and exits 0.
12 | 
13 | Usage:
14 |     python prepare_cache_megacpp.py [--data-root ...] [--dataset-name ...]
15 | """
16 | 
17 | from __future__ import annotations
18 | 
19 | import argparse
20 | import os
21 | import sys
22 | from pathlib import Path
23 | 
24 | DEFAULT_DATA_ROOT = os.environ.get(
25 |     "MEGACPP_DATA_ROOT", "/home/dave/cppmega-root/data"
26 | )
27 | DEFAULT_DATASET_NAME = os.environ.get(
28 |     "MEGACPP_DATASET_NAME", "clang_semantic_4k_v10"
29 | )
30 | 
31 |

  4 | Checks:
  5 |   1. ``<prefix>_train.bin`` and ``<prefix>_train.idx`` exist and are non-empty.
  6 |   2. ``.idx`` parses (via megatron-core if available, else raw struct check).
  7 |   3. Token-ID range lies within expected vocab (default 131072).
  8 |   4. Document count and total-token count are printed.
  9 |   5. First 64 tokens of document 0 are printed for sanity.

 11 | Exits non-zero on failure (no silent fallbacks).

 13 | Usage:
 14 |     python verify_dataset_megacpp.py
 15 |     python verify_dataset_megacpp.py --vocab-size 131072

 36 | def _raw_idx_inspect(idx_path: Path) -> tuple[int, int]:
 37 |     """Minimal MMIDIDX .idx parser — matches the fallback writer in
 38 |     ``data_prep_parquet_to_megatron.py``. Returns (num_docs, dtype_code)."""

 40 |         magic = f.read(9)
 41 |         if magic != b"MMIDIDX\x00\x00":
 42 |             raise RuntimeError(f"bad magic in {idx_path}: {magic!r}")
 43 |         (version,) = struct.unpack("<Q", f.read(8))
 44 |         (dtype_code,) = struct.unpack("<B", f.read(1))
 45 |         (num_sequences,) = struct.unpack("<Q", f.read(8))
 46 |     return num_sequences, dtype_code
 47 | 
 48 | 
 49 | def main() -> int:
 50 |     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
 51 |     parser.add_argument("--data-root", default=DEFAULT_DATA_ROOT)
 52 |     parser.add_argument("--dataset-name", default=DEFAULT_DATASET_NAME)
 53 |     parser.add_argument("--vocab-size", type=int, default=131072)

 64 |         prefix = megatron_dir / f"{args.dataset_name}_{suffix}"
 65 |         bin_path = prefix.with_suffix(".bin")
 66 |         idx_path = prefix.with_suffix(".idx")

 68 |         if not bin_path.is_file():
 69 |             sys.exit(f"ERROR: missing {bin_path}")
 70 |         if not idx_path.is_file():
 71 |             sys.exit(f"ERROR: missing {idx_path}")
 72 |         bin_bytes = bin_path.stat().st_size
 73 |         idx_bytes = idx_path.stat().st_size
 74 |         print(f"  .bin={bin_bytes/1024**3:.2f} GiB  .idx={idx_bytes/1024**2:.2f} MiB")
 75 |         if bin_bytes == 0:

 90 |             arr_mm = np.memmap(bin_path, dtype=sample.dtype, mode="r")

 97 |                 )

 99 |         except Exception as e:
100 |             print(f"  megatron-core unavailable ({e}); falling back to raw idx check")
101 |             n_docs, dtype_code = _raw_idx_inspect(idx_path)
102 |             print(f"  raw: num_sequences={n_docs:,} dtype_code={dtype_code}")

  1 | #!/usr/bin/env python3
  2 | """Convert nanochat-style tokenized parquet to Megatron indexed binary format.
  3 | 
  4 | Reads ``token_ids`` (uint32) from parquet shards and writes ``.bin`` + ``.idx``
  5 | files that Megatron's GPTDataset / MMapIndexedDataset can consume directly.
  6 | 
  7 | This script must run on the H200 machine where megatron-core is installed.
  8 | 
  9 | Usage:
 10 |     python data_prep_parquet_to_megatron.py \
 11 |         --input-dir /home/dave/cppmega-root/data/parquet/clang_semantic_4k_v10 \
 12 |         --output-prefix /home/dave/cppmega-root/data/megatron/clang_semantic_4k_v10 \
 13 |         --split train
 14 | 
 15 |     python data_prep_parquet_to_megatron.py \
 16 |         --input-dir /home/dave/cppmega-root/data/parquet/clang_commits_4k_v1 \
 17 |         --output-prefix /home/dave/cppmega-root/data/megatron/clang_commits_4k_v1 \
 18 |         --split train

 21 | from __future__ import annotations
 22 | 
 23 | import argparse
 24 | import os
 25 | import sys
 26 | import time
 27 | from pathlib import Path
 28 | 
 29 | import numpy as np
 30 | 
 31 | 
 32 | _OUTPUT_DTYPE_MAP = {
 33 |     "uint8": np.uint8,
 34 |     "uint16": np.uint16,
 35 |     "int32": np.int32,
 36 |     "int64": np.int64,
 37 |     # Historical CLI compatibility. Megatron's MMIDIDX dtype enum has no
 38 |     # uint32 token dtype, so positive token IDs that need more than uint16 must
 39 |     # be stored as int32.
 40 |     "uint32": np.int32,
 41 | }
 42 | 
 43 | _MEGATRON_DTYPE_CODE_MAP = {
 44 |     np.uint8: 1,
 45 |     np.int32: 4,
 46 |     np.int64: 5,
 47 |     np.uint16: 8,
 48 | }
 49 | 
 50 | 
 51 | def _resolve_output_dtype(dtype_str: str) -> type[np.generic]:
 52 |     try:
 53 |         dtype = _OUTPUT_DTYPE_MAP[dtype_str]
 54 |     except KeyError as exc:
 55 |         raise ValueError(f"unsupported dtype: {dtype_str}") from exc
 56 |     if dtype_str == "uint32":
 57 |         print(
 58 |             "WARNING: Megatron MMIDIDX has no uint32 dtype code; "
 59 |             "writing token IDs as int32 instead",
 60 |             file=sys.stderr,
 61 |         )
 62 |     return dtype
 63 | 
 64 | 
 65 | def _megatron_dtype_code(dtype: type[np.generic] | np.dtype) -> int:
 66 |     dtype_type = np.dtype(dtype).type
 67 |     if dtype_type not in _MEGATRON_DTYPE_CODE_MAP:
 68 |         supported = ", ".join(
 69 |             sorted(
 70 |                 np.dtype(supported_dtype).name
 71 |                 for supported_dtype in _MEGATRON_DTYPE_CODE_MAP
 72 |             )
 73 |         )
 74 |         raise ValueError(
 75 |             f"unsupported Megatron MMIDIDX dtype {np.dtype(dtype).name}; "
 76 |             f"supported dtypes: {supported}"
 77 |         )
 78 |     return _MEGATRON_DTYPE_CODE_MAP[dtype_type]

 81 | def find_parquet_shards(input_dir: str, split: str) -> list[str]:
 82 |     """Find all parquet shard files for a given split.
 83 | 
 84 |     Convention from nanochat:
 85 |     - train shards: shard_00000.parquet ... shard_NNNNN.parquet (all except last)
 86 |     - val shard: val_shard.parquet or last shard
 87 |     """
 88 |     input_path = Path(input_dir)
 89 |     all_parquets = sorted(input_path.glob("*.parquet"))
 90 |     if not all_parquets:
 91 |         raise FileNotFoundError(f"no parquet files in {input_dir}")
 92 |

 95 |

 98 |             return [str(p) for p in all_parquets if p.name != "val_shard.parquet"]
 99 |         # Last shard is val by convention
100 |         return [str(p) for p in all_parquets[:-1]] if len(all_parquets) > 1 else [str(all_parquets[0])]
101 |     elif split == "val":
102 |         if has_explicit_val:
103 |             return [str(val_shard)]
104 |         return [str(all_parquets[-1])] if len(all_parquets) > 1 else [str(all_parquets[0])]
105 |     else:

124 |             then sizes[num_docs] as int32, then pointers[num_docs] as int64

129 |     dtype = _resolve_output_dtype(dtype_str)
130 |     dtype_code = _megatron_dtype_code(dtype)

143 |     t0 = time.time()

145 |     columns_to_read = [token_column] + (side_channels or [])

147 |     for shard_idx, shard_path in enumerate(shards):

171 |                         all_side_docs[col].append(np.array(side_val, dtype=side_dtypes[col]))
172 |         if (shard_idx + 1) % 10 == 0:

178 |     bin_path = output_prefix + ".bin"

243 | def convert_parquet_to_megatron(
244 |     input_dir: str,
245 |     output_prefix: str,

304 |     t0 = time.time()
305 | 
306 |     columns_to_read = [token_column] + (side_channels or [])
307 | 
308 |     for shard_idx, shard_path in enumerate(shards):
309 |         pf = pq.ParquetFile(shard_path)

312 |             token_col = table.column(token_column)

314 |             for row_idx in range(len(token_col)):

345 |             f"{total_docs:,} docs, {total_tokens:,} tokens "

 89 | def _get_absolute_token_indices(dataset: Any, idx: int) -> np.ndarray:
 90 |     """Reconstruct absolute token-level indices inside the flat bin file for the given sequence."""
 91 |     if dataset.shuffle_index is None:
 92 |         # Lazy memmap the indexes if not loaded yet
 93 |         dataset.shuffle_index = np.load(
 94 |             dataset.path_to_shuffle_index, allow_pickle=True, mmap_mode='r'
 95 |         )
 96 |         dataset.sample_index = np.load(
 97 |             dataset.path_to_sample_index, allow_pickle=True, mmap_mode='r'
 98 |         )
 99 |         dataset.document_index = np.load(
100 |             dataset.path_to_document_index, allow_pickle=True, mmap_mode='r'
101 |         )
102 | 
103 |     # Perform shuffle mapping
104 |     shuffled_idx = dataset.shuffle_index[idx]
105 | 
106 |     # Get beginning and end documents and offsets
107 |     doc_index_beg, doc_index_beg_offset = dataset.sample_index[shuffled_idx]
108 |     doc_index_end, doc_index_end_offset = dataset.sample_index[shuffled_idx + 1]
109 | 
110 |     token_itemsize = np.dtype(dataset.dataset.index.dtype).itemsize
111 | 
112 |     if doc_index_beg == doc_index_end:
113 |         # Sequence spans a single document
114 |         doc_start_token = dataset.dataset.index.sequence_pointers[doc_index_beg] // token_itemsize
115 |         start = doc_start_token + doc_index_beg_offset
116 |         length = doc_index_end_offset - doc_index_beg_offset + dataset.config.add_extra_token_to_sequence
117 |         return np.arange(start, start + length, dtype=np.int64)
118 |     else:
119 |         # Sequence spans multiple documents
120 |         parts = []
121 |         for i in range(doc_index_beg, doc_index_end + 1):
122 |             doc_start_token = dataset.dataset.index.sequence_pointers[i] // token_itemsize
123 |             if i == doc_index_beg:
124 |                 start = doc_start_token + doc_index_beg_offset
125 |                 length = dataset.dataset.index.sequence_lengths[i] - doc_index_beg_offset
126 |             elif i == doc_index_end:
127 |                 start = doc_start_token
128 |                 length = doc_index_end_offset + dataset.config.add_extra_token_to_sequence
129 |             else:
130 |                 start = doc_start_token
131 |                 length = dataset.dataset.index.sequence_lengths[i]
132 |             parts.append(np.arange(start, start + length, dtype=np.int64))
133 |         return np.concatenate(parts)

## File: /Volumes/external/sources/cppmega/docs/data_preparation.md

- Extension: .md
- Language: markdown
- Size: 9539 bytes
- Created: 2026-05-22 12:02:49
- Modified: 2026-05-22 12:02:49

### Code

```markdown
  1 | # megacpp data preparation pipeline
  2 | 
  3 | End-to-end recipe for producing the Megatron-format dataset that
  4 | `scripts/remote_smoke_h200_dsa_9_4_m.sh` (and every other NAM56R launcher)
  5 | reads via `--data-path`.
  6 | 
  7 | All stages live under `scripts/data/` and are orchestrated by
  8 | `scripts/data/prepare_data.sh`.
  9 | 
 10 | ```
 11 | scripts/data/
 12 | ├── prepare_data.sh                           # master dispatcher
 13 | ├── prepare_download_megacpp.sh               # stage 1: clone C/C++ repos
 14 | ├── prepare_tokenize_megacpp.py               # stage 2: clang index + BPE tokenize -> parquet
 15 | ├── prepare_stream_jsonl_to_parquet_megacpp.py  #   helper (self-contained)
 16 | ├── prepare_format_megacpp.py                 # stage 3: parquet -> Megatron .bin/.idx
 17 | ├── prepare_cache_megacpp.py                  # stage 4: warm index cache
 18 | └── verify_dataset_megacpp.py                 # stage 5: sanity-check
 19 | ```
 20 | 
 21 | ---
 22 | 
 23 | ## Source data
 24 | 
 25 | **Corpus:** eight public C/C++ repositories cloned shallow:
 26 | 
 27 | | repo | ref | purpose |
 28 | |---|---|---|
 29 | | `llvm/llvm-project` | `llvmorg-19.1.0` | modern C++, compilers |
 30 | | `boostorg/boost`   | `boost-1.86.0` (+submodules) | template-heavy C++ |
 31 | | `torvalds/linux`   | `v6.10` | C, systems |
 32 | | `fmtlib/fmt`       | `11.0.0` | small high-quality C++ |
 33 | | `google/googletest`| `v1.15.0` | test patterns |
 34 | | `abseil/abseil-cpp`| tip        | Google C++ commons |
 35 | | `facebook/folly`   | tip        | Facebook C++ |
 36 | | `grpc/grpc`        | `v1.67.0` | large C++ service framework |
 37 | 
 38 | **License + provenance:** all sources are public on GitHub under their
 39 | respective upstream licenses (Apache 2.0 for LLVM/abseil/grpc, BSL-1.0 for
 40 | Boost, GPL-2.0 for Linux kernel headers, MIT for fmt/googletest,
 41 | Apache 2.0 for folly). No credentials required to clone.
 42 | 
 43 | **Size:** shallow clones total ~15 GB on disk; after filtering to
 44 | C/C++/header files the usable corpus is several hundred thousand files.
 45 | Exact token count depends on tokenizer + filtering — `verify_dataset_megacpp.py`
 46 | prints it at the end.
 47 | 
 48 | ---
 49 | 
 50 | ## Tokenizer
 51 | 
 52 | **Vocab:** 131 072 tokens (aligned with `--vocab-size` in training launchers
 53 | and with the nanochat reference).
 54 | 
 55 | **Style:** hybrid fixed C++ vocabulary + learned BPE with BERT-style
 56 | whitespace handling. Implemented in nanochat's `nanochat/cpp_tokenizer.py`
 57 | (HuggingFace `tokenizers` backend).
 58 | 
 59 | **Artifact:** `tokenizer.json` (~2.2 MiB).
 60 | `prepare_tokenize_megacpp.py` copies it from
 61 | `${MEGACPP_NANOCHAT_ROOT}/tokenizer.json` into
 62 | `${MEGACPP_DATA_ROOT}/tokenizer/tokenizer.json` so the launcher's
 63 | `--tokenizer-model "${REMOTE_ROOT}/data/tokenizer"` can find it.
 64 | 
 65 | > **Note:** the tokenizer artifact is *not* vendored inside cppmega — it
 66 | > is a binary artifact owned by the nanochat repo. Set
 67 | > `MEGACPP_NANOCHAT_ROOT` to point at a local nanochat checkout.
 68 | 
 69 | ---
 70 | 
 71 | ## Pipeline
 72 | 
 73 | ### Stage 1 — download
 74 | ```bash
 75 | bash scripts/data/prepare_data.sh download
 76 | # or directly:
 77 | bash scripts/data/prepare_download_megacpp.sh
 78 | ```
 79 | Shallow-clones the eight repos into `${MEGACPP_DATA_ROOT}/cpp_raw/`.
 80 | Idempotent — re-running skips existing directories.
 81 | 
 82 | ### Stage 2 — tokenize (requires nanochat)
 83 | ```bash
 84 | export MEGACPP_NANOCHAT_ROOT=/path/to/nanochat
 85 | python scripts/data/prepare_tokenize_megacpp.py
 86 | ```
 87 | Dispatches to `nanochat/scripts/data/run_clang_pipeline.sh`, which:
 88 | 1. Runs libclang-based semantic indexing over each project.
 89 | 2. Emits enriched JSONL (one doc per semantic chunk, ≤4096 tokens).
 90 | 3. Tokenizes with the hybrid BPE tokenizer.
 91 | 4. Streams into parquet shards of 50k docs each, plus a `val_shard.parquet`.
 92 | 5. Writes `_COMPLETE` sentinel.
 93 | 
 94 | Output: `${MEGACPP_DATA_ROOT}/parquet/clang_semantic_4k_v10/`.
 95 | 
 96 | **Why the nanochat dependency?** The clang indexer and tokenizer modules
 97 | (`nanochat/tools/clang_indexer/`, `nanochat/nanochat/cpp_tokenizer.py`,
 98 | `nanochat/nanochat/tokenized_enriched*`) are several thousand lines each
 99 | and pull in libclang bindings. Vendoring them into cppmega would duplicate
100 | a maintained upstream. See `scripts/data/prepare_tokenize_megacpp.py`
101 | header for the exact file list.
102 | 
103 | ### Stage 3 — format (parquet → Megatron `.bin`/`.idx`)
104 | ```bash
105 | python scripts/data/prepare_format_megacpp.py
106 | ```
107 | Writes both splits:
108 | - `${MEGACPP_DATA_ROOT}/megatron/clang_semantic_4k_v10_train.{bin,idx}`
109 | - `${MEGACPP_DATA_ROOT}/megatron/clang_semantic_4k_v10_valid.{bin,idx}`
110 | 
111 | Uses `int32` output tokens (vocab=131072 > 65535 so `uint16` is invalid;
112 | Megatron MMIDIDX has no `uint32` dtype code).
113 | Implementation lives in `scripts/data_prep_parquet_to_megatron.py` which
114 | prefers `megatron.core.datasets.indexed_dataset.IndexedDatasetBuilder`
115 | and falls back to a raw `MMIDIDX` writer when megatron-core isn't
116 | available.
117 | 
118 | ### Stage 4 — cache
119 | ```bash
120 | python scripts/data/prepare_cache_megacpp.py
121 | ```
122 | Validates the `.bin`/`.idx` pair via `megatron.core.datasets.indexed_dataset.IndexedDataset`
123 | and reports `docs`, `tokens`, `dtype`. On dev laptops without
124 | megatron-core installed this stage logs a SKIP and exits 0.
125 | 
126 | Megatron's own `GPTDataset` sample-index lives at
127 | `${MEGACPP_DATA_ROOT}/megatron/cache/GPTDataset_indices/` and is built at
128 | the first training launch — we rely on Megatron to manage it rather than
129 | pre-building here (sample index depends on seed / seq-length / global
130 | batch size and is cheap to regenerate).
131 | 
132 | ### Stage 5 — verify
133 | ```bash
134 | python scripts/data/verify_dataset_megacpp.py
135 | ```
136 | Checks `.bin`/`.idx` exist + non-empty, parses the index, verifies
137 | `max(token_id) < vocab_size` (default 131072), prints the first 64 tokens
138 | of document 0. Non-zero exit on any failure — **no silent fallbacks**.
139 | 
140 | ---
141 | 
142 | ## Megatron data format
143 | 
144 | - `.bin` — flat packed token IDs (default dtype `int32` for vocab=131072).
145 | - `.idx` — `MMIDIDX\x00\x00` magic + version + dtype-code + document count +
146 |   `sizes[int32]` + `pointers[int64]` + `doc_idx[int64]`. Matches the
147 |   `megatron-core` `MMapIndexedDataset` reader.
148 | - On-disk layout:
149 |   ```
150 |   ${MEGACPP_DATA_ROOT}/
151 |   ├── cpp_raw/…                       # stage 1
152 |   ├── parquet/clang_semantic_4k_v10/  # stage 2
153 |   │   ├── shard_00000.parquet
154 |   │   ├── …
155 |   │   ├── val_shard.parquet
156 |   │   └── _COMPLETE
157 |   ├── tokenizer/tokenizer.json        # stage 2 copy
158 |   └── megatron/                       # stage 3
159 |       ├── clang_semantic_4k_v10_train.bin
160 |       ├── clang_semantic_4k_v10_train.idx
161 |       ├── clang_semantic_4k_v10_valid.bin
162 |       ├── clang_semantic_4k_v10_valid.idx
163 |       └── cache/GPTDataset_indices/   # built at first training launch
164 |   ```
165 | 
166 | ---
167 | 
168 | ## How to point training at this data
169 | 
170 | `scripts/remote_smoke_h200_dsa_9_4_m.sh` (and siblings) hard-code:
171 | 
172 | ```bash
173 | --data-path 1.0 "${REMOTE_ROOT}/data/megatron/clang_semantic_4k_v10_train" \
174 | --tokenizer-type HuggingFaceTokenizer \
175 | --tokenizer-model "${REMOTE_ROOT}/data/tokenizer" \
176 | --split 98,1,1 \
177 | ```
178 | 
179 | so as long as `${REMOTE_ROOT}/data/` matches `${MEGACPP_DATA_ROOT}`
180 | (bench3: `/mnt/data/cppmega-root/data`, europe:
181 | `/home/dave/cppmega-root/data`) the launcher picks it up without change.
182 | 
183 | To override at launch time without editing the script, patch the
184 | `--data-path` argument in an `EXTRA_FLAGS` wrapper or hand-edit the
185 | launcher block.
186 | 
187 | ---
188 | 
189 | ## Storage requirements
190 | 
191 | | stage | artifact | approx size |
192 | |---|---|---|
193 | | 1 | raw clones (`cpp_raw/`) | ~15 GB |
194 | | 2 | enriched JSONL (transient) | ~20-30 GB |
195 | | 2 | parquet shards | ~8-12 GB |
196 | | 3 | `.bin` train+valid | ~6-10 GB |
197 | | 3 | `.idx` train+valid | <100 MiB |
198 | | 4 | Megatron sample cache | <1 GiB (built at training launch) |
199 | 
200 | Ranges depend on how much of each repo survives the "compilable / parseable"
201 | filter inside the clang indexer.
202 | 
203 | ---
204 | 
205 | ## Reproducibility
206 | 
207 | - **Pinned refs:** every repo URL in `prepare_download_megacpp.sh` carries
208 |   an explicit tag (`llvmorg-19.1.0`, `v6.10`, `boost-1.86.0`, …).
209 |   Shallow clones mean the exact commit is determined by the remote tag —
210 |   there is a small risk of retagging upstream; mirror the raw corpus
211 |   tarball if absolute reproducibility matters.
212 | - **Tokenizer version:** tied to the nanochat commit you point
213 |   `MEGACPP_NANOCHAT_ROOT` at. Record that commit hash together with any
214 |   checkpoint.
215 | - **Deterministic preprocessing:** the streaming parquet writer uses a
216 |   fixed `--seed=42`; the clang indexer is order-sensitive on file-system
217 |   enumeration and is NOT guaranteed bitwise-reproducible across kernels.
218 |   For audits, hash the resulting `.bin` file:
219 |   ```
220 |   sha256sum ${MEGACPP_DATA_ROOT}/megatron/clang_semantic_4k_v10_train.bin
221 |   ```
222 |   and pin that hash in the experiment log.
223 | 
224 | ---
225 | 
226 | ## Honesty notes / gaps
227 | 
228 | - **Nanochat dep:** stage 2 dispatches into
229 |   `nanochat/scripts/data/run_clang_pipeline.sh` rather than re-implementing
230 |   the clang indexer + tokenizer inside cppmega. This is intentional —
231 |   vendoring ~thousands of LoC of actively-maintained tokenizer code would
232 |   be worse than a path dependency on the upstream checkout. If that
233 |   coupling is unacceptable, the alternative is a clean-room
234 |   re-implementation of the indexer; budget accordingly.
235 | - **No pre-built cache in stage 4:** Megatron's GPTDataset sample index
236 |   depends on `--seed`, `--seq-length`, `--global-batch-size`, and
237 |   `--train-iters`; pre-building it in a separate stage would be fragile
238 |   and Megatron rebuilds it in seconds anyway. Stage 4 only warms the
239 |   `.bin`/`.idx` memmap and validates integrity.
240 | - **Raw corpus not versioned:** `cpp_raw/` is ~15 GB and lives outside
241 |   git. If you need to reproduce a run after upstream repos change, mirror
242 |   `cpp_raw/` to cold storage before discarding.
```

```markdown
  1 | # Data Pipeline Design
  2 | 
  3 | **Status**: Mixed roadmap/history document. This file is not the current
  4 | operational source of truth for the implemented pipeline.
  5 | **Related bd epic**: `cpp-data-pipeline`
  6 | **Design doc**: `docs/design/02-data-pipeline.md`
  7 | 
  8 | Current source of truth:
  9 | 
 10 | - implemented pipeline/runtime behavior: `docs/DATA_PIPELINE.md`
 11 | - actual loaders and packing behavior: `nanochat/dataloader.py`
 12 | - active corpus builders: `tools/cpp_chunker/`, `tools/clang_indexer/`, and
 13 |   `scripts/data/*`
 14 | 
 15 | Read this document primarily as roadmap / acquisition / design intent. Several
 16 | sections below describe planned or partially explored dataset/tooling directions
 17 | rather than the current in-repo operational path.
 18 | 
 19 | ---
 20 | 
 21 | ## Principle: Use Existing Libraries, Don't Reinvent
 22 | 
 23 | | Task                       | Library / Dataset                                                                                                 | Build Custom? |
 24 | | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
 25 | | Pipeline framework         | [DataTrove](https://github.com/huggingface/datatrove) (HuggingFace)                                               | No            |
 26 | | Code quality filters       | [bigcode-dataset](https://github.com/bigcode-project/bigcode-dataset)                                             | No            |
 27 | | Near-deduplication         | [datasketch](https://github.com/ekzhu/datasketch) + BigCode MinHash script                                        | No            |
 28 | | PII removal                | [bigcode/pii-lib](https://github.com/bigcode-project/pii-lib) + [StarPII](https://huggingface.co/bigcode/starpii) | No            |
 29 | | Secret detection           | [Yelp/detect-secrets](https://github.com/Yelp/detect-secrets)                                                     | No            |
 30 | | License detection          | ScanCode Toolkit                                                                                                  | No            |
 31 | | Tokenizer training         | [HuggingFace tokenizers](https://github.com/huggingface/tokenizers)                                               | No            |
 32 | | Pre-processed C++ data     | `nvidia/Nemotron-Pretraining-Code-v1+v2`                                                                          | No            |
 33 | | C++ open-source code       | `bigcode/the-stack-dedup` (data/c++)                                                                              | No            |
 34 | | C++ pre-tokenization regex | Custom (~50 lines)                                                                                                | Yes           |
 35 | | Indentation stripping      | Custom (~30 lines)                                                                                                | Yes           |
 36 | | FIM data transform         | Custom (~20 lines)                                                                                                | Yes           |
 37 | | Binary .bin/.idx packaging | Custom (match nanochat format)                                                                                    | Yes           |
 38 | | Compilation rate evaluator | Custom                                                                                                            | Yes           |
 39 | 
 40 | ---
 41 | 
 42 | ## Data Budget
 43 | 
 44 | | Model      | Params | Chinchilla Optimal | Our Target  | Epochs on 80B unique |
 45 | | ---------- | ------ | ------------------ | ----------- | -------------------- |
 46 | | Dense 3B   | 3B     | 60B tokens         | 300B tokens | 3.75                 |
 47 | | MoE 12B/2B | 12B    | 240B tokens        | 300B tokens | 3.75                 |
 48 | 
 49 | Target: **300-400 billion tokens** total throughput.
 50 | 
 51 | ---
 52 | 
 53 | ## Source Code Acquisition
 54 | 
 55 | ### Pre-Processed Datasets (Use Directly — Already Deduped/Filtered)
 56 | 
 57 | **HuggingFace Token**: Set `HF_TOKEN` env var (see `.env` or ask maintainer)
 58 | 
 59 | | Dataset                 | HF Path                               | C++                                | Size          | Quality                                  |
 60 | | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
 61 | | **Nemotron Code v1**    | `nvidia/Nemotron-Pretraining-Code-v1` | Yes                                | ~747B tokens  | Highest (multi-stage filter + synthetic) |
 62 | | **Nemotron Code v2**    | `nvidia/Nemotron-Pretraining-Code-v2` | Yes (+ code review, transpilation) | 897GB         | Highest                                  |
 63 | | **Nemotron CC Code v1** | `nvidia/Nemotron-CC-Code-v1`          | Yes                                | 428B tokens   | High (LLM quality-scored)                |
 64 | | **The Stack (dedup)**   | `bigcode/the-stack-dedup`             | Yes (`data/c++`)                   | ~3TB total    | Good (MinHash deduped)                   |
 65 | | **CommitPack**          | `bigcode/commitpack`                  | Yes (C++ subset)                   | ~4TB total    | Good (git commit+diff pairs)             |
 66 | | **CommitPackFT**        | `bigcode/commitpackft`                | Yes (C++ subset)                   | ~2GB filtered | High (quality-filtered commits)          |
 67 | 
 68 | ### Raw Sources (Supplement for Diversity)
 69 | 
 70 | | Source                               | Size (raw)         | Language | Download Method                        |
 71 | | ------------------------------------ | ------------------ | -------- | -------------------------------------- |
 72 | | **Linux Kernel**                     | ~1.2GB per version | C        | `git clone` by tag (v6.0, v6.6, v6.10) |
 73 | | **LLVM/Clang**                       | ~2GB               | C++      | `git clone` by release tag (17-19)     |
 74 | | **GCC**                              | ~1.5GB             | C, C++   | `git clone` (13-14)                    |
 75 | | **Boost**                            | ~800MB per version | C++      | GitHub releases (1.84-1.86)            |
 76 | | **CUDA Toolkit** (samples + headers) | ~500MB             | C, C++   | NVIDIA developer downloads (12.x)      |
 77 | | **STL implementations**              | ~200MB             | C++      | libstdc++ (GCC), libc++ (LLVM)         |
 78 | | **Chromium**                         | ~30GB              | C++      | `depot_tools` fetch                    |
 79 | | **Qt Framework**                     | ~2GB               | C++      | `git clone`                            |
 80 | 
 81 | ### Download Scripts
 82 | 
 83 | Each source gets a version-pinned download script in `scripts/data/`:
 84 | 
 85 | ```bash
 86 | scripts/data/
 87 | ├── download_stack_v2.py       # HuggingFace streaming download
 88 | ├── download_linux_kernel.sh   # git clone specific tags
 89 | ├── download_llvm.sh           # git clone release branches
 90 | ├── download_gcc.sh            # git clone or mirror
 91 | ├── download_boost.sh          # GitHub release tarballs
 92 | ├── download_cuda_samples.sh   # NVIDIA download
 93 | ├── download_stl.sh            # libstdc++ and libc++
 94 | └── download_all.sh            # Master script
 95 | ```
 96 | 
 97 | ### Version Strategy
 98 | 
 99 | Pin to recent stable releases to get modern C++ (C++17/20/23):
100 | - Linux Kernel: v6.0, v6.6, v6.10
101 | - LLVM: 17.x, 18.x, 19.x
102 | - GCC: 13.x, 14.x
103 | - Boost: 1.84, 1.85, 1.86
104 | - CUDA: 12.x headers and samples
105 | 
106 | ---
107 | 
108 | ## Deduplication
109 | 
110 | ### Why Deduplication is Critical
111 | 
112 | GitHub contains massive duplication:
113 | - Forked repositories (same code, different repos)
114 | - Copy-pasted utility files (json.hpp, stb_image.h)
115 | - Vendored dependencies (entire libraries copied into repos)
116 | 
117 | Without dedup: model memorizes popular libraries, loses generalization.
118 | 
119 | ### Method: MinHash + LSH
120 | 
121 | ```
122 | Pipeline:
123 | Raw files → Shingling (5-grams) → MinHash (128 hashes) → LSH (20 bands × 6 rows)
124 |                                                             ↓
125 |                                                     Cluster duplicates
126 |                                                             ↓
127 |                                                     Keep 1 per cluster
128 | ```
129 | 
130 | **Tools**: `datasketch` library or custom implementation.
131 | 
132 | **Parameters**:
133 | - Jaccard threshold: 0.7 (files sharing >70% content are duplicates)
134 | - Shingle size: 5 tokens (after normalization)
135 | - MinHash permutations: 128
136 | 
137 | ### Exact Dedup
138 | 
139 | Additionally, SHA-256 hash exact duplicates (identical files across repos).
140 | 
141 | ### Expected Results
142 | 
143 | | Stage                      | Size        |
144 | | -------------------------- | ----------- |
145 | | Raw C/C++ from all sources | ~500GB text |
146 | | After exact dedup          | ~350GB      |
147 | | After MinHash near-dedup   | ~150-200GB  |
148 | | After quality filtering    | ~120-150GB  |
149 | | Unique tokens (estimated)  | ~60-80B     |
150 | 
151 | ---
152 | 
153 | ## Code Normalization ("The Flattener")
154 | 
155 | ### Algorithm
156 | 
157 | ```python
158 | import re
159 | 
160 | def normalize_cpp(code: str) -> str:
161 |     """Normalize C++ code for training.
162 | 
163 |     - Strip leading whitespace (indentation)
164 |     - Preserve newlines
165 |     - Compress multiple blank lines to one
166 |     - Preserve comments
167 |     - Preserve string literals
168 |     """
169 |     lines = code.split('\n')
170 |     result = []
171 |     prev_blank = False
172 | 
173 |     for line in lines:
174 |         stripped = line.strip()
175 |         if not stripped:
176 |             if not prev_blank:
177 |                 result.append('')
178 |                 prev_blank = True
179 |             continue
180 |         prev_blank = False
181 |         result.append(stripped)
182 | 
183 |     return '\n'.join(result)
184 | ```
185 | 
186 | ### Before/After Example
187 | 
188 | **Before** (raw source):
189 | ```cpp
190 | void ProcessPacket(Packet* p) {
191 |     // Validate input
192 |     if (!p) {
193 |         LOG_ERROR("Null packet");
194 |         return;
195 |     }
196 | 
197 |     if (p->size() > MAX_SIZE) {
198 |         LOG_WARN("Oversized packet");
199 |         return;
200 |     }
201 | 
202 |     dispatch(p);
203 | }
204 | ```
205 | 
206 | **After** (normalized):
207 | ```cpp
208 | void ProcessPacket(Packet* p) {
209 | // Validate input
210 | if (!p) {
211 | LOG_ERROR("Null packet");
212 | return;
213 | }
214 | 
215 | if (p->size() > MAX_SIZE) {
216 | LOG_WARN("Oversized packet");
217 | return;
218 | }
219 | 
220 | dispatch(p);
221 | }
222 | ```
223 | 
224 | ---
225 | 
226 | ## Quality Filtering
227 | 
228 | ### Heuristic Filters
229 | 
230 | | Filter                    | Threshold                                         | Rationale                        |
231 | | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
232 | | Max file size             | 1MB                                               | Auto-generated files, data dumps |
233 | | Max line length           | 1000 chars                                        | Minified code, embedded data     |
234 | | Min file size             | 100 bytes                                         | Empty/trivial files              |
235 | | Min unique lines ratio    | >30%                                              | Repetitive boilerplate           |
236 | | Max comment-to-code ratio | <80%                                              | Files that are mostly comments   |
237 | | Has valid C++ extension   | `.c`, `.cc`, `.cpp`, `.cxx`, `.h`, `.hpp`, `.hxx` | Correct language                 |
238 | 
239 | ### Content Filters
240 | 
241 | | Filter                 | Method                                  | Rationale                         |
242 | | ---------------------- | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
243 | | License headers        | Regex detect + strip first N lines      | Wastes context, no semantic value |
244 | | Auto-generated markers | Detect `// Generated by`, `DO NOT EDIT` | Bad training signal               |
245 | | Binary/hex dumps       | Entropy check (>4.5 bits/byte in ASCII) | Not useful code                   |
246 | | Test data files        | Detect `.test.cpp` with only data       | Low code quality                  |
247 | | Vendored deps          | Detect common vendored dirs             | Already in primary sources        |
248 | 
249 | ### PII Redaction
250 | 
251 | Replace with placeholder tokens:
252 | - Email addresses → `user@example.com`
253 | - IP addresses → `127.0.0.1`
254 | - API keys (high-entropy strings) → `API_KEY_REDACTED`
255 | - File paths with usernames → `/home/user/`
256 | 
257 | ---
258 | 
259 | ## FIM Augmentation
260 | 
261 | ### Fill-In-the-Middle Format
262 | 
263 | 50% of training examples use FIM format:
264 | 
265 | ```
266 | Original:  AAAA BBBB CCCC
267 | FIM Input: <FIM_PREFIX> AAAA <FIM_SUFFIX> CCCC <FIM_MIDDLE> BBBB <EOS>
268 | ```
269 | 
270 | ### Split Strategy
271 | 
272 | For each file selected for FIM:
273 | 1. Choose random split point (uniform over character positions)
274 | 2. Split into prefix, middle, suffix
275 | 3. Middle length: 10-50% of file (random)
276 | 4. Concatenate in PSM order (Prefix-Suffix-Middle)
277 | 
278 | ### Implementation
279 | 
280 | ```python
281 | import random
282 | 
283 | def create_fim_example(code: str, fim_rate: float = 0.5) -> str:
284 |     if random.random() > fim_rate:
285 |         return code  # Normal NTP
286 | 
287 |     # Random split point
288 |     split1 = random.randint(0, len(code))
289 |     split2 = random.randint(split1, len(code))
290 | 
291 |     prefix = code[:split1]
292 |     middle = code[split1:split2]
293 |     suffix = code[split2:]
294 | 
295 |     return f"<FIM_PREFIX>{prefix}<FIM_SUFFIX>{suffix}<FIM_MIDDLE>{middle}<EOS>"
296 | ```
297 | 
298 | ---
299 | 
300 | ## Data Mix
301 | 
302 | ### Training Data Composition
303 | 
304 | | Source                          | Fraction | Tokens (est.) | Purpose                             |
305 | | ------------------------------- | -------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------- |
306 | | Clean GitHub C++                | 60%      | 180-240B      | Diverse real-world code             |
307 | | Synthetic textbooks             | 20%      | 60-80B        | Concepts, best practices, reasoning |
308 | | Code exercises (LeetCode-style) | 10%      | 30-40B        | Problem → Solution patterns         |
309 | | Instruction Q&A                 | 10%      | 30-40B        | Question → Reasoning → Code format  |
310 | 
311 | ### Synthetic Data Generation
312 | 
313 | Use a teacher model (Claude/GPT-4) to generate:
314 | 
315 | 1. **Textbook examples**: "Explain RAII with code example" → `// QUESTION:` + `/* ANSWER */` + code
316 | 2. **Bug-fix pairs**: Inject bug into good code → generate debug trace → write fix
317 | 3. **Code review**: "What's wrong with this code?" → reasoning + fixed version
318 | 
319 | ### Multi-Epoch Strategy
320 | 
321 | With ~80B unique tokens and 300B target:
322 | - Epoch 1-2: Full corpus, standard order
323 | - Epoch 3-4: Re-shuffled, different FIM splits
324 | - Never repeat exact same FIM split of same file
325 | 
326 | ---
327 | 
328 | ## Binary Packaging
329 | 
330 | ### Output Format
331 | 
332 | Pre-tokenized binary files compatible with nanochat's `binary_distributed_data_loader`:
333 | 
334 | ```
335 | File format:
336 | [8 bytes: uint64 num_tokens] [num_tokens × uint16 token_ids]
337 | ```
338 | 
339 | ### Pipeline
340 | 
341 | ```
342 | Raw C++ files
343 |     → normalize_cpp()
344 |     → quality_filter()
345 |     → deduplicate()
346 |     → create_fim_example() (50% chance)
347 |     → tokenizer.encode()
348 |     → write to .bin file
349 | ```
350 | 
351 | ### Sharding
352 | 
353 | - Shard size: ~1GB each (~300M tokens per shard)
354 | - Train shards: 900+ files
355 | - Validation shard: Last shard (held out)
356 | - Index file (`.idx`): Maps shard → token count for efficient seeking
357 | 
358 | ---
359 | 
360 | ## Validation Split
361 | 
362 | - **Size**: 1% of total data (~3B tokens)
363 | - **Composition**: Same mix ratio as training data
364 | - **Constraint**: No file appears in both train and validation
365 | - **Purpose**: Monitor bits-per-byte during training
366 | 
367 | ---
368 | 
369 | ## Enriched Parquet Format (Structure-Aware Training)
370 | 
371 | ### Problem Statement
372 | 
373 | The Rust `cpp-chunker` computes rich structural metadata (call graphs, dependency
374 | levels, type hierarchies, scope boundaries) during processing, but ALL of it is
375 | discarded at the `OutputRecord` boundary — the model only sees flat text.
376 | 
377 | ### Design: Variant C (Full Learned)
378 | 
379 | We chose the smartest approach: both structure embeddings at input AND learned
380 | relation bias in attention, all through backpropagation.
381 | 
382 | Important current caveat:
383 | 
384 | - several chunk-generation paths still budget document size by rough
385 |   `chars / 4` estimates inside `tools/cpp_chunker`, commit extraction, and some
386 |   enrichment scripts.
387 | - current training/runtime defaults use the C++ tokenizer
388 |   (`nanochat/tokenizer.py` -> `CppTokenizer`) rather than that heuristic.
389 | - therefore dataset suffixes like `4k`, `8k`, `16k`, `64k` should be treated as
390 |   target buckets, not exact tokenizer-length guarantees, unless a specific
391 |   artifact family has been re-measured with the current tokenizer.
392 | 
393 | **New parquet columns** (backward-compatible — `text` column unchanged):
394 | 
395 | | Column | Type | Purpose |
396 | |--------|------|---------|
397 | | `structure_ids` | `list<u8>` | Per-character structure category (9 types: preamble, func_sig, func_body, class_decl, class_member, comment, typedef, namespace, other) |
398 | | `chunk_boundaries` | `list<struct{start, end, kind, name, dep_level}>` | Chunk-level metadata (char-indexed offsets) |
399 | | `call_edges` | `list<struct{from, to}>` | Intra-document call graph edges |
400 | | `type_edges` | `list<struct{from, to}>` | Type dependency edges |
401 | | `ast_depth` | `list<u8>` | Per-character AST nesting depth |
402 | | `sibling_index` | `list<u8>` | Per-character sibling index |
403 | | `ast_node_type` | `list<u8>` | Per-character AST node-type bucket |
404 | 
405 | **Input-level integration:**
406 | ```python
407 | h = token_emb + position_emb + structure_emb[structure_ids] + dep_level_emb[dep_levels]
408 | ```
409 | 
410 | **Attention-level integration:**
411 | ```python
412 | # Per-relation learnable bias per head (like ALiBi but structure-aware)
413 | bias[i,j] = sum(relation_weight[r, head] for r in relations_between(i, j))
414 | # Current relation set is explicit and chunk-level:
415 | # SAME_CHUNK, CALLER_CALLEE, CALLEE_CALLER, TYPE_DEPENDENCY,
416 | # TYPE_DEPENDENT, SAME_DEP_LEVEL, ADJACENT_DEP_LEVEL,
417 | # PREAMBLE_TO_CODE, CODE_TO_PREAMBLE
418 | ```
419 | 
420 | **Engram benefits automatically** — receives enriched hidden states, no changes needed.
421 | 
422 | ### Implementation Plan
423 | 
424 | 1. **Rust**: `cpp-chunker` already emits enriched columns for the active enriched paths
425 | 2. **Python dataloader**: Read new columns, convert char-offset → token-offset
426 | 3. **Model**: Add structure/dep_level embedding tables, learned relation bias
427 | 4. **Graceful fallback**: Missing columns → standard flat-text training
```

12 | ## 2. Graph Dataset v4 (Tree-sitter Context Graph)

14 | *   **Status**: **RUNNING HEALTHY (100% CPU utilization)**.

Enables the model to learn code structure through backpropagation (Variant C: structure embeddings at input + learned relation bias in attention).

26 | ## 4. Обогащённый набор v6 (Structure-Aware Parquet)
27 | *   **Описание**: Расширенный формат parquet, который сохраняет структурные метаданные из Rust-тулчейна `cpp-chunker` — категории структуры для каждого символа (9 типов), границы чанков с уровнями зависимостей, рёбра графа вызовов и рёбра зависимостей типов. Модель учится структуре кода через backpropagation (Вариант C: эмбеддинги структуры на входе + обучаемое смещение attention по структурным связям).

30 | *   **Где будет лежать**: `gs://nanochat-training-data-2026/data/cpp_enriched_16k/` и `cpp_enriched_64k/`.

  1 | """
  2 | Train the C++ hybrid tokenizer: fixed C++ vocab + learned BPE, BERT-style whitespace.
  3 | 
  4 | Usage:
  5 |     python -m scripts.tok_train_cpp [--input data/cpp_clean.jsonl] [--vocab_size 65536] [--max_chars 5000000000]
  6 | 
  7 | See docs/design/01-tokenizer.md for full design.
  8 | 
  9 | Fixed vocabulary structure (4800 tokens, IDs 0-4799):
 10 |     - IDs 0-19: Special tokens (20)
 11 |     - IDs 20-199: C++ keywords (180)
 12 |     - IDs 200-399: Operators (200)
 13 |     - IDs 400-499: Preprocessor (100)
 14 |     - IDs 500-699: Punctuation (200)
 15 |     - IDs 700-3699: STL/Standard library functions (3000)
 16 |     - IDs 3700-4699: Numbers 0-999 (1000)
 17 |     - IDs 4700-4799: Reserved (100)
 18 |     - IDs 4800-65535: Learned BPE (60736)
 19 | """
 20 | import os
 21 | import json
 22 | import time
 23 | import argparse
 24 | from typing import Protocol, cast
 25 | 
 26 | from tokenizers import Tokenizer, Regex
 27 | from tokenizers.models import BPE
 28 | from tokenizers.trainers import BpeTrainer
 29 | from tokenizers.pre_tokenizers import Sequence, Split, WhitespaceSplit
 30 | 
 31 | 
 32 | # =============================================================================
 33 | # Load Fixed Vocabulary from JSON
 34 | # =============================================================================
 35 | 
 36 | def load_fixed_vocab(vocab_path: str) -> list[str]:
 37 |     """Load fixed vocabulary from JSON file. Returns ordered list where index = token ID."""
 38 |     with open(vocab_path, 'r') as f:
 39 |         vocab_dict = json.load(f)
 40 |     # Sort by ID to get ordered list
 41 |     max_id = max(vocab_dict.values())
 42 |     fixed_tokens = [''] * (max_id + 1)
 43 |     for token, id_ in vocab_dict.items():
 44 |         fixed_tokens[id_] = token
 45 |     return fixed_tokens
 46 | 
 47 | 
 48 | def build_fixed_tokens(vocab_path: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
 49 |     """Build ordered list of all fixed tokens. Index = token ID."""
 50 |     if vocab_path is None:
 51 |         # Default path relative to script location
 52 |         script_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
 53 |         vocab_path = os.path.join(script_dir, '..', 'data', 'cpp_tokenizer', 'fixed_vocab.json')
 54 |     return load_fixed_vocab(vocab_path)
 55 | 
 56 | 
 57 | # =============================================================================
 58 | # Pre-tokenizer: BERT-style whitespace + C++ operator isolation
 59 | # =============================================================================
 60 | 
 61 | CPP_PRE_TOKENIZER_PATTERN = r"""(?x)
 62 |     # Multi-char operators (longest match first)
 63 |     <=>|<<=|>>=|->\*|\.\*|
 64 |     ::|->|==|!=|<=|>=|&&|\|\||<<|>>|\+\+|--|
 65 |     \+=|-=|\*=|/=|%=|&=|\|=|\^=|
 66 |     \.\.\.|\#\#|//|/\*|\*/|
 67 |     # Diff markers
 68 |     \@\@|---|\+\+\+|
 69 |     # Newlines (structural whitespace token)
 70 |     \n\n|\n|
 71 |     # Single-char punctuation (each is its own token)
 72 |     [{}()\[\]<>;:,.\+\-\*/%&\|^~!?=\#@\$_\\\"'`]
 73 | """
 74 | 
 75 | def build_pre_tokenizer():
 76 |     """BERT-style: isolate fixed patterns then split on whitespace."""
 77 |     return Sequence([
 78 |         Split(Regex(CPP_PRE_TOKENIZER_PATTERN), behavior="isolated"),
 79 |         WhitespaceSplit(),
 80 |     ])
 81 | 
 82 | 
 83 | class _TokenizerWithPreTokenizer(Protocol):
 84 |     pre_tokenizer: object
 85 | 
 86 | 
 87 | class _BpeTrainerFactory(Protocol):
 88 |     def __call__(
 89 |         self,
 90 |         *,
 91 |         vocab_size: int,
 92 |         min_frequency: int,
 93 |         special_tokens: list[str],
 94 |         show_progress: bool,
 95 |     ) -> BpeTrainer: ...
 96 | 
 97 | 
 98 | # =============================================================================
 99 | # Text iterator from JSONL
100 | # =============================================================================
101 | 
102 | def text_iterator(input_path: str, max_chars: int, doc_cap: int = 10_000):
103 |     nchars = 0
104 |     with open(input_path, 'r') as f:
105 |         for line in f:
106 |             if not line.strip():
107 |                 continue
108 |             record = json.loads(line)
109 |             text = record.get('text', '')
110 |             if len(text) > doc_cap:
111 |                 text = text[:doc_cap]
112 |             nchars += len(text)
113 |             yield text
114 |             if nchars >= max_chars:
115 |                 return
116 |     print(f"Read {nchars:,} chars from {input_path}")
117 | 
118 | 
119 | # =============================================================================
120 | # Main: train tokenizer
121 | # =============================================================================
122 | 
123 | def main():
124 |     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Train C++ hybrid BPE tokenizer')
125 |     parser.add_argument('--input', default='data/cpp_clean.jsonl', help='Input JSONL file')
126 |     parser.add_argument('--output_dir', default='data/cpp_tokenizer', help='Output directory')
127 |     parser.add_argument('--vocab_size', type=int, default=65536, help='Total vocab size (default: 65536)')
128 |     parser.add_argument('--max_chars', type=int, default=5_000_000_000, help='Max chars to train on')
129 |     parser.add_argument('--doc_cap', type=int, default=10_000, help='Max chars per document')
130 |     parser.add_argument('--min_frequency', type=int, default=2, help='Min BPE merge frequency')
131 |     parser.add_argument('--fixed_vocab', default=None, help='Path to fixed_vocab.json (default: data/cpp_tokenizer/fixed_vocab.json)')
132 |     args = parser.parse_args()
133 | 
134 |     # Resolve paths relative to project root
135 |     project_root = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..'))
136 |     input_path = os.path.join(project_root, args.input)
137 |     output_dir = os.path.join(project_root, args.output_dir)
138 |     os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
139 | 
140 |     # Resolve fixed vocab path
141 |     if args.fixed_vocab:
142 |         fixed_vocab_path = args.fixed_vocab
143 |     else:
144 |         fixed_vocab_path = os.path.join(output_dir, 'fixed_vocab.json')
145 | 
146 |     print(f"Input: {input_path}")
147 |     print(f"Output: {output_dir}")
148 |     print(f"Fixed vocab: {fixed_vocab_path}")
149 |     print(f"Vocab size: {args.vocab_size}")
150 |     print(f"Max chars: {args.max_chars:,}")
151 | 
152 |     # Build fixed tokens from JSON
153 |     fixed_tokens = build_fixed_tokens(fixed_vocab_path)
154 |     print(f"Fixed tokens: {len(fixed_tokens)}")
155 |     print(f"Learned BPE slots: {args.vocab_size - len(fixed_tokens)}")
156 | 
157 |     # Initialize tokenizer
158 |     tokenizer = Tokenizer(BPE(unk_token="<UNK>"))
159 |     cast(_TokenizerWithPreTokenizer, tokenizer).pre_tokenizer = build_pre_tokenizer()
160 | 
161 |     # Train BPE
162 |     trainer = cast(_BpeTrainerFactory, BpeTrainer)(
163 |         vocab_size=args.vocab_size,
164 |         min_frequency=args.min_frequency,
165 |         special_tokens=fixed_tokens,  # These get IDs 0..1599 in order
166 |         show_progress=True,
167 |     )
168 | 
169 |     print("\n=== Training BPE ===")
170 |     t0 = time.time()
171 |     text_iter = text_iterator(input_path, args.max_chars, args.doc_cap)
172 |     tokenizer.train_from_iterator(text_iter, trainer=trainer)
173 |     t1 = time.time()
174 |     print(f"Training time: {t1 - t0:.1f}s")
175 |     print(f"Vocab size: {tokenizer.get_vocab_size()}")
176 | 
177 |     # Save
178 |     tokenizer_path = os.path.join(output_dir, "tokenizer.json")
179 |     tokenizer.save(tokenizer_path)
180 |     print(f"Saved to {tokenizer_path}")
181 | 
182 |     # === Validation ===
183 |     print("\n=== Validation ===")
184 |     validate(tokenizer, fixed_tokens)
185 | 
186 | 
187 | def validate(tokenizer, fixed_tokens):
188 |     """Run validation checks for the tokenizer."""
189 |     fixed_map = {tok: i for i, tok in enumerate(fixed_tokens) if tok}
190 | 
191 |     tests = [
192 |         # (input, description, expected_properties)
193 |         ("std::vector<int>", "STL template", {
194 |             "max_tokens": 7,  # std :: vector < int > (6 meaningful)
195 |         }),
196 |         ("nullptr", "keyword as single token", {
197 |             "exact_tokens": 1,
198 |         }),
199 |         ("return 42;", "keyword + number + punct", {
200 |             "max_tokens": 5,
201 |         }),
202 |         ("cout << endl", "stream output", {
203 |             "max_tokens": 5,
204 |         }),
205 |         ("if (!buf) return;", "null check pattern", {
206 |             "max_tokens": 10,
207 |         }),
208 |         ("cudaMalloc(&ptr, size)", "CUDA API call", {
209 |             "max_tokens": 10,
210 |         }),
211 |         ("std::unique_ptr<T>", "smart pointer", {
212 |             "max_tokens": 7,
213 |         }),
214 |     ]
215 | 
216 |     all_passed = True
217 |     for text, desc, props in tests:
218 |         enc = tokenizer.encode(text)
219 |         ids = enc.ids
220 |         tokens = enc.tokens
221 |         print(f"\n  {desc}: \"{text}\"")
222 |         print(f"    Tokens ({len(ids)}): {tokens}")
223 |         print(f"    IDs: {ids}")
224 | 
225 |         if "exact_tokens" in props and len(ids) != props["exact_tokens"]:
226 |             print(f"    FAIL: expected {props['exact_tokens']} tokens, got {len(ids)}")
227 |             all_passed = False
228 |         if "max_tokens" in props and len(ids) > props["max_tokens"]:
229 |             print(f"    FAIL: expected <= {props['max_tokens']} tokens, got {len(ids)}")
230 |             all_passed = False
231 | 
232 |     # Check fixed token IDs
233 |     print("\n  Fixed token ID checks:")
234 |     checks = [
235 |         # (token, category, expected_id_range_start, expected_id_range_end)
236 |         ("::", "operator", 200, 400),
237 |         ("->", "operator", 200, 400),
238 |         ("nullptr", "keyword", 20, 200),
239 |         ("return", "keyword", 20, 200),
240 |         ("std", "STL name", 700, 3700),
241 |         ("vector", "STL name", 700, 3700),
242 |         ("cudaMalloc", "CUDA API", 700, 3700),
243 |         ("42", "number", 3700, 4700),
244 |         ("0", "number", 3700, 4700),
245 |         ("999", "number", 3700, 4700),
246 |     ]
247 |     vocab = tokenizer.get_vocab()
248 |     for tok, cat, range_start, range_end in checks:
249 |         if tok in fixed_map:
250 |             expected_id = fixed_map[tok]
251 |             actual_id = vocab.get(tok, -1)
252 |             in_range = range_start <= actual_id < range_end
253 |             status = "OK" if actual_id == expected_id and in_range else f"MISMATCH (expected {expected_id}, got {actual_id})"
254 |             print(f"    {tok!r:20s} ({cat:10s}) ID={actual_id:5d} {status}")
255 |             if actual_id != expected_id:
256 |                 all_passed = False
257 |         else:
258 |             print(f"    {tok!r:20s} ({cat:10s}) NOT in fixed vocab!")
259 |             # Not a failure if not in fixed vocab - might be learned
260 | 
261 |     # Decode test
262 |     print("\n  Decode test:")
263 |     test_code = "int main() {\nreturn 0;\n}"
264 |     enc = tokenizer.encode(test_code)
265 |     decoded = tokenizer.decode(enc.ids)

   1 | #!/usr/bin/env python3
   2 | """Analyze proposed tokenizer v3 vocabulary frequency in C++ training corpus.
   3 | 
   4 | Validates proposed fixed vocabulary tokens from TOKENIZER_V2_PROPOSAL.md against
   5 | actual usage in the cpp_compilable training dataset. Reports per-category coverage
   6 | and per-token frequency to guide fixed vocab allocation.
   7 | 
   8 | Usage:
   9 |     # Analyze single shard (fast, ~2 min)
  10 |     python -m scripts.data.analyze_vocab_frequency /tmp/shard_00000.parquet
  11 | 
  12 |     # Analyze multiple shards
  13 |     python -m scripts.data.analyze_vocab_frequency /tmp/shard_0000*.parquet
  14 | 
  15 |     # Filter by category
  16 |     python -m scripts.data.analyze_vocab_frequency /tmp/shard_00000.parquet -c cuda
  17 | 
  18 |     # Show morpheme analysis
  19 |     python -m scripts.data.analyze_vocab_frequency /tmp/shard_00000.parquet --morphemes
  20 | 
  21 |     # JSON output for downstream processing
  22 |     python -m scripts.data.analyze_vocab_frequency /tmp/shard_00000.parquet --json -o results.json
  23 | """
